newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.
newsitem.headline: Mideast and African port conditions - Lloyds.

text.p: Port conditions from Lloyds Shipping Intelligence Service --

ANGOLA, Jan 23 - Luanda - Four vessels awaiting berth. Current berthing delays for genral cargo vessels is 6 days, no delays for container,ro-ro or product tankers. The main cargoes affected by delays are aid cargoes. Lobito, Namibe - No delays reported.

ISRAEL, Jan 28 - Haifa - Two vessels due, 1-2 days delay expected. Loading/discharging at berth, general cargo, 1 bulk, 5 containers, 1 tanker, 1 passenger vessel. Waiting at anchorage to load/discharge, 2 bulk, 1 container vessel, 1 tanker, 2 vessels under repair, 2 awaiting orders. Ashdod - 2-4 Days delay expected. Loading/discharging at berth, 12 general cargo, 1 bulk, 2 containers. Waiting at anchorage to load/discharge, 19 general cargo, 1 bulk, 1 passenger. Eilat - Loading/discharging at berth, 1 bulk, 1 container vessel.

MOZAMBIQUE, Jan 27 - Nacala - Port working normally (first come, first served basis). No restriction on berthing and sailing during night time. Draft restriction of 9.5 metres plus height of tide at general cargo berths and 14 metres at container berths. One tugboat available. Beira - General cargo berths - Working normally (first come, first served basis). Container terminal/other terminals - Working normally. Pilotage is now possible 24 hours a day for vessels up to 140 metres loa with a maximum draft of 7.5 metres. Two tugboats now fully operational. Night navigation for larger vessels is restricted and subject to prior arrangements with the port captain. Maputo - Pilotage is now poss
NAMIBIA, Jan 27 - Walvis Bay - Working normally.

NIGERIA, Jan 28 - Lagos - One vessel with import cargo discharging. Port Harcourt - No berthing delays reported. Bonny, Forcados - The dispute by SPDC junior staff is reported to have been resolved, and no delays reported. All other crude terminals reported as operating normally.

SOUTH AFRICA, Jan 27 - Richards Bay - general cargo/bulk import berths working normally. Bulk export berths - delays of 24-48 hours for the coming week. 1 belt route will be under repair from 0600 hrs 27/1 to 1800 hours. Bulk coal - 9 Vessels at outer anchorage, 4 alongside, 12 due. Berthing delays 36-48 hours. Durban container terminal delays of up to 60 hours. Berths and terminals working normally. Bunker supply delays 8 hours due to bunching of vessels. East London - General cargo/combi terminal berths working normally. Port Elizabeth - Working normally/no delays. Cape Town - No berthing delays. Saldanha Bay - Working normally.

TUNISIA, Jan 25 - Gabes - Two tankers loading at berth, 2 vessels discharging at berth (1 bulk sulphur, 1 bulk spath flour). Tunis - Three vessels in port of which 1 awaiting instructions. Rades - Three ro-ro vessels in port. Goulette - North side - 3 vessels of which 1 soyabean tanker, 1 general cargo, 1 passenger. South side - 2 Vessels discharging of which 1 grain, 1 lab syrene tanker, 2 vessels in roads. Sfax - Six vessels operating of which 2 discharging timber, 1 discharging bulk sulphur, 1 discharging bulk wheat, 1 discharging general cargo, 1 loading bulk olive kernels. Sousse - One vessel discharging general cargo. No waiting time.

UNITED ARAB EMIRATES, Jan 27 - Dubai - Containers, 26 vessels due, 4 loading at berth. General cargo, 9 vessels due, 4 discharging at berth, 1 under repair/laid up. Tankers, 3 vessels due, 1 vessel discharging at berth ,9 under repair/laid up.

YEMEN, Jan 26 - Hodeidah - All berths are occupied, 5 vessels alongside of which 3 bulk wheat, 1 sugar, 1 wheat flour, 1 container vessel, 1 general cargo. 2 Vessels anchored of which 1 containers, 1 general cargo. Berthing delays, up to 2 days for general cargo, up to 4 days for bagged cargo, up to 6 days for bulk cargo, up to 1 day for containers. Mokha - One vessel alongside discharging wheat flour, no vessels anchored, no waiting time.
